responses.content: The Higgs boson was experimentally confirmed in **July 2012**. The confirmation came from the **Large Hadron Collider (LHC)** at CERN, where the **ATLAS** and **CMS** experiments observed a new particle with a mass of approximately **125 GeV**. This discovery was announced on **July 4, 2012**, by CERN scientists, marking the first direct observation of the Higgs boson, a key component of the Standard Model of particle physics. Subsequent studies in the years that followed further validated its properties, solidifying its role in explaining how particles acquire mass.
